question: True or false: Turkey may charge merchant ships a toll for passing through the Bosphorus?
answer: False. The Montreux Convention of 1936 gives merchant ships free passage in peacetime; Turkey may charge only fixed fees for lighthouses, sanitary control and rescue services. So one of the busiest straits on earth earns its owner little, while Egypt took about $10 billion from the Suez Canal in 2023.
move: Owning the gate is worth only what the treaties let you charge.
trap: Carrying over the Suez and Panama model of paying to pass.
reference: Convention Regarding the Regime of the Straits, signed at Montreux, 20 July 1936
